name: John Christopher Sullivan
current_role: Executive Vice President, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary, Costco Wholesale Corp.
profile: John Sullivan is Costco's top lawyer. He has been Corporate Secretary since 2010 and General Counsel since 2016, and he became an executive officer in 2021. He leads the legal function at the Issaquah, WA-based warehouse retailer. His reported wealth comes from Costco equity disclosed in SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: Costco's 10-K says he has been Corporate Secretary since 2010 and General Counsel since 2016. He was named an executive officer (EVP) in 2021. In a 2014 SEC letter he signed as VP, Associate General Counsel & Secretary.
notes: Low-profile in-house lawyer with almost no public interviews. A common name: several other lawyers called John Sullivan (TI China, Carlson Inc.) show up in searches, so don't mix them up. Best route is Costco corporate or IR.

name: Rahul Ghai
current_role: Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, GE Aerospace (General Electric Co.)
profile: Rahul Ghai has been CFO of GE Aerospace since August 2022. He was also CFO of all of GE from September 2023 until the GE Vernova spin-off in April 2024. Before GE he was CFO of Otis, where he helped with its spin-off from UTC, and before that CFO of Harris Corp. for four years. He earlier held finance roles at Aetna, Carrier and UTC Fire & Security. His wealth comes from executive equity compensation.
interesting_fact: He has now helped steer three big corporate separations: Otis's spin-off from United Technologies, GE Vernova's spin-off from GE, and GE's own transformation into a standalone GE Aerospace.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in financial services in India. He earned an undergraduate degree in accounting and economics from Delhi University before getting an MBA from Purdue. GE credits his four years as CFO of Harris Corp. in Florida with tripling its stock price.
notes: Public-company CFO and a regular on earnings calls. As CFO he oversees investor relations, so the GE Aerospace IR team (Head of IR: Blaire Shoor) is the natural route. Directly relevant to the energy theme through the GE Vernova spin.

name: Ryan Greenawalt
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Alta Equipment Group Inc. (NYSE: ALTG)
profile: Ryan Greenawalt is the second-generation leader of Alta Equipment. His father Steve founded it in 1984 as a single Yale forklift dealership in Detroit. Ryan rejoined in 2008 after several years in wealth management, led the move into construction equipment and many acquisitions, bought out the family in 2017, and took Alta public in February 2020. He still runs it as Chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: In 2009, in the middle of Michigan's auto-industry crisis, he led Alta's purchase of a Volvo construction-equipment dealership directly from the factory. That deal took the forklift dealer into construction equipment.
deep_cut_fact: After the University of Michigan and an MBA at Michigan State, he left the family business in 2002 and spent about seven years in wealth management in San Francisco. He returned to Detroit in December 2008. He has said the industry's real bottleneck is talent, because 'there are not enough people coming into the trades today.'
notes: Founder-family CEO of a mid-cap dealer that also runs a material-handling and electrification/power-equipment business. IR is handled by an outside firm (Kevin Inda, SCR Partners). Speaks at Detroit Smart Business dealmaker events.

name: Bruno Augusto Sacchi Zaremba
current_role: President of Finance and Operations (CFO/COO), Vinci Compass Investments Ltd. (Nasdaq: VINP)
profile: Bruno Zaremba is a Brazilian investor and partner at Vinci Compass, the Rio-based alternative asset manager formerly called Vinci Partners. He started at Banco Pactual and led Vinci's private equity business from 2007. After the merger with Compass he became CFO/COO, overseeing finance, operations, corporate development and shareholder relations. His wealth comes from his partnership stake.
interesting_fact: He began in 1996 as an equity analyst at Banco Pactual covering banks, beverages, retail, food and tobacco. In 2002 he moved to managing Pactual's proprietary equity and debt investments in the US and was made a partner.
deep_cut_fact: He is a CFA charterholder with an economics degree from PUC-Rio. He spent his early years at Banco Pactual, the bank where Vinci's founding partners worked before they left to start Vinci in 2009.
notes: Brazil-based. Third-party sites give conflicting education details; the firm's own page (PUC-Rio economics, CFA, HBS alumnus) is used here. Older profiles list him as Head of IR or Co-Head of PE. The 'founding partners from Pactual in 2009' context is general firm history, not specific to him.

name: James D Taiclet Jr
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Lockheed Martin Corp.
profile: Jim Taiclet is a Pittsburgh-born former US Air Force pilot. He worked at McKinsey, Pratt & Whitney and Honeywell Aerospace Services, then ran American Tower as CEO from 2003 to 2020 and built it into a global cell-tower REIT. He has been CEO of Lockheed Martin since June 2020 and chairman since 2021, and he pushes a '21st Century Security' agenda of digital and networked defense technology.
interesting_fact: Harvard Business Review named him one of the world's 'Best-Performing CEOs' every year from 2013 to 2018, for his run at American Tower.
deep_cut_fact: He captained the rugby team in his senior year at the US Air Force Academy (class of 1982). As an Air Force pilot during Operation Desert Shield he flew missions in a Lockheed C-141 Starlifter, a Lockheed-built jet, decades before he ran the company.
notes: Very high-profile defense CEO with heavily managed access, so go through Lockheed Corporate Communications. He sits on the Council on Foreign Relations board. His telecom-infrastructure background at American Tower is relevant to data centers.

name: Michael Bosco
current_role: Partner, Investment Team, North Run Capital, LP (Boston)
profile: Mike Bosco is a partner on the investment team at North Run Capital, a Boston firm managing more than $300M that takes concentrated convertible-preferred stakes in small and micro-cap public companies. He shows up as a LightPath Technologies insider ('Other') because he is a limited partner in North Run's NR-DNP fund, which holds LightPath shares (13D filed Feb 2025). He was briefly a director of Creative Realities in November 2025.
interesting_fact: North Run's 2025 deal with LightPath, an optics and infrared-imaging maker, was a convertible-preferred-plus-warrants investment. His stated insider role at LightPath comes from that fund holding, not from an operating job.
deep_cut_fact: North Run nominated him to the Creative Realities board on 6 Nov 2025. He resigned on 19 Nov 2025 so the company would stay within Nasdaq's change-of-control rule while shareholders voted on North Run's preferred-stock conversion.
notes: Identity is matched through SEC filings: 'Bosco Michael' (CIK 2058718) files jointly with North Run on LightPath. A different filer, 'Bosco Michael Louis' (CIK 2073654), at Pursuit Attractions may be another person. The $33M figure probably reflects fund holdings attributed to him, not personal wealth. Web search budget ran out, so the bio is from filings and the firm site only.

name: Jennifer Newstead
current_role: SVP, General Counsel and Government Affairs, Apple Inc. (also a director of Emerson Electric)
profile: Jennifer Newstead is a US lawyer. She was a Davis Polk partner for 12 years, then State Department Legal Adviser in 2017–19. She spent six years as Facebook/Meta's general counsel and then chief legal officer, and led Meta's defense in the 2025 FTC antitrust trial, which Meta won. She joined Apple in January 2026 and became General Counsel on 1 March, running a combined Legal and Government Affairs group. Her wealth comes from Meta and Apple equity.
interesting_fact: She was the first woman to serve as Legal Adviser of the US State Department. In 2018 she argued for the United States as agent and counsel before the International Court of Justice in Iran v. United States.
deep_cut_fact: After Yale Law School she clerked for Judge Laurence Silberman on the DC Circuit and then for Justice Stephen Breyer at the Supreme Court. She has also taught as an adjunct professor at Georgetown Law.
notes: Joined Emerson's board in Aug 2026. Apple corporate communications is tightly controlled and I found no verified general press email (search budget ran out). Expect access only through Apple PR. She is said to have helped draft the Patriot Act while at DOJ, which can be a sensitive topic.

name: Michael Louis Battles
current_role: Co-CEO & Co-President, Clean Harbors Inc. (retiring 31 Dec 2026, then strategic adviser in 2027); director, Casella Waste Systems
profile: Mike Battles is a CPA and University of Vermont graduate. He trained at Deloitte and held senior finance roles at PerkinElmer, including Chief Accounting Officer and acting CFO. He joined Clean Harbors in 2013 as Chief Accounting Officer, was CFO from 2016 and Co-CEO from March 2023. In October 2026 the company said he will retire at year-end, leaving Eric Gerstenberg as sole CEO.
interesting_fact: In announcing his retirement, Clean Harbors' chairman said that under the Battles/Gerstenberg co-CEO setup since 2023 the hazardous-waste firm posted record results and more than tripled its stock price.
deep_cut_fact: Early at Deloitte he was posted to the firm's national-office accounting research group. He also holds a Certificate in Cybersecurity Oversight from the NACD and Carnegie Mellon University.
notes: In transition: he leaves the CEO role and the Clean Harbors board on 31 Dec 2026. That could make him more available for a podcast in 2027, as an adviser and Casella director. Clean Harbors runs incinerators and re-refineries (Safety-Kleen), which fits the energy theme.

name: Adam Edward Wible
current_role: Co-founder of Nu Holdings (Nubank); CTO 2013–2021, then moved to work on technology platforms (current title not verified)
profile: Edward Wible is the American co-founder of Nubank, the Brazil-based digital bank started in 2013 with David Vélez and Cristina Junqueira. He was CTO for about eight years. In April 2021 he left the CTO role to work more directly on building the company's systems and infrastructure. As a named founder he holds high-vote Class B shares in Nu Holdings (NYSE: NU), which went public in December 2021.
interesting_fact: Vélez recruited Wible on the advice of Sequoia Capital, Nubank's seed investor. Under his technology leadership Nubank bought Cognitect in 2020, the company behind the Clojure programming language and the Datomic database that Nubank's systems run on.
notes: Goes by Edward Wible. Very low public profile. Web search budget ran out before I could verify his current role and background, so check before outreach. Best route is Nu press. 'Alive' is marked unknown only because nothing recent was checked; there is no indication otherwise.

name: Girish Mathrubootham
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Together Fund (AI/SaaS venture fund); founder of Freshworks
profile: Girish Mathrubootham is a former Zoho executive. In 2010 he co-founded Freshdesk, later Freshworks, in Chennai with Shan Krishnasamy, and took it public on Nasdaq in 2021 as one of India's flagship SaaS companies. He handed the CEO role to Dennis Woodside in 2024 and then became executive chairman. He is no longer listed on Freshworks' board and now invests in AI-first software founders through Together Fund, which he co-founded with Manav Garg.
interesting_fact: In his 2021 IPO founder letter he listed the doubts he had heard: '600 help desks in the market', 'you can't find talent in Chennai', and 'you can't build a global SaaS company from India'. He chose to stay in Chennai anyway.
deep_cut_fact: His IPO founder letter opens with 'I feel really good today', the text of an artwork on the wall of Freshworks' Chennai office. He says he showed a picture of it at almost every company meeting to remind staff they choose how they approach their work.
notes: Together Fund lists him as US-based. Very active in the Indian SaaS community (SaaSBoomi) and generally approachable for founder-focused podcasts. The Zoho litigation (settled 2021) is a topic to avoid.

name: Valery Nebesny
current_role: Listed as a co-founder of BitFury (Bitfury Group); current role not verified
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists name Valery Nebesny as a co-founder of BitFury, the bitcoin-mining hardware and data-center company led by co-founder Valery Vavilov. Bitfury now calls itself a technology incubator spanning Web3, high-performance computing and AI. Its current team page does not list Nebesny, and I could not verify his present role.
notes: Very low public profile. Bitfury's current board lists Val Vavilov (CEO, Chairman), Brian P. Brooks, George Kikvadze and Bertrand des Pallieres, but not Nebesny. The web search budget ran out and Wikipedia has no article on Bitfury or him, so identity and status could not be checked further. Bitfury's HPC and AI data-center pivot fits the podcast theme, but the company contact is the only route found.

name: Peter Diamandis
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, XPRIZE Foundation; co-founder of Singularity University, Abundance360, BOLD Capital Partners and Fountain Life; co-founder & vice chairman, Human Longevity Inc.
profile: Peter Diamandis is a Greek-American MIT engineer and Harvard MD who has founded more than 25 companies in space, longevity, venture capital and education. He launched the $10M Ansari XPRIZE, which SpaceShipOne won in 2004. He co-founded Human Longevity Inc. with Craig Venter. Today he runs the XPRIZE Foundation and its $101M Healthspan prize, the Abundance360 community and BOLD Capital, and he hosts the Moonshots podcast.
interesting_fact: He created the XPRIZE after reading Charles Lindbergh's 'The Spirit of St. Louis', taking Lindbergh's Orteig Prize as his model. The prize was announced in St. Louis in 1996 before any purse money or teams existed. The winning SpaceShipOne now hangs in the Smithsonian next to the Spirit of St. Louis.
deep_cut_fact: He won first place in a rocket-design competition at age 12. As a medical student he co-founded International MicroSpace, a small-satellite launcher that won a $100M SDIO contract but was sold in 1993 for just $250,000. That failure helped prompt him to start XPRIZE.
notes: Very media-friendly and runs his own podcast. His site names Connie Fox at XPRIZE as the contact for speaking and media requests, which is the best route. His interests in energy abundance and AI data centers fit the show well.

name: Marc Spiegel
current_role: Founder & Managing Member, Innovatio Capital LLC; majority owner of Querétaro F.C.; independent director, Columbus Circle Capital Corp II (SPAC, now Inflection Point Acquisition Corp. VII)
profile: Marc Spiegel grew up in his family's waste-hauling businesses, which were sold to Republic Services and Waste Management. In 2009 he co-founded Rubicon Technologies, a cloud-based waste and recycling marketplace that became a unicorn and went public via SPAC in 2022, and he stayed until 2024. He now invests through Innovatio Capital, founded the 502Circle NIL collective in 2022, and owns Mexican Liga MX club Querétaro F.C.
interesting_fact: He is the majority owner of Querétaro F.C., a top-flight Mexican soccer club. That fits a background in sport: he has a BS in Sport Administration from the University of Louisville.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 he founded 502Circle, an NIL collective that lets communities financially support student-athletes; 502 is Louisville's area code. He holds both a BS and an MPA in non-profit management from the University of Louisville, and was on the Atlanta Business Chronicle's 40 Under 40 list in 2016.
notes: No published personal or office contact found, and the web search budget ran out. The 502Circle domain now redirects to a Louisville Cardinals fan site. Possible routes are Querétaro F.C. media relations or the SPAC (Inflection Point VII). Avoid Rubicon's post-SPAC decline as a topic.
